description.narrative: Project-level impacts: Stakeholders Effect Increased access to finance for microfinance clients, including farmers: The Project will provide the Bank with an efficient risk mitigation tool, so it can continue to sustainably provide access to finance to MF clients, who are perceived to have a higher risk profile post 2022 floods and thus help increase/stabilize their economic activities. Market-level Impacts: Resilience: The Project anticipates filling an important market gap by providing a risk sharing facility to HBL MFB, which is one of the largest microfinance providers in the country. This in turn will contribute to improving the resilience and confidence in the microfinance sector via a demonstration effect, and will enable the scaling up micro, and small ticket financing catering to microenterprises and borrowers in the country. This is likely to encourage other microfinance players to continue expanding their microfinance portfolios, particularly amidst a challenging macroeconomic environment.

The proposed project consists of a Risk Sharing Facility (RSF) for an aggregate portfolio of up to US$80 million in equivalent Pakistani Rupees (PKR) with HBL Microfinance Bank (HBL MFB or the Bank) in Pakistan (the Project). The Project aims to support HBL MFB as part of IFC's response to rehabilitate the microfinance (MF) sector post the impact of the 2022 floods and ongoing macro-political challenges. The Project is expected to be supported by the Private Sector Window of Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP). IFCs exposure will be up to US$40 million, or 50% of the risk sharing facility.
